subject: Ephemeral SSO link expired mid-audit — request for auto-reclaim policy & bridge letter
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@diligencepartners.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@diligencepartners.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Access interruption during evidence download — request for extension and policy clarification

Hi Kimberly,

During our reviewer session this morning the ephemeral SSO link to the trust portal timed out while we were mid-download of the SOC 2 bundle. We were able to re-request access, but it interrupted the QA samples and we lost our position in the evidence queue.

Two asks: 1) could you reissue a one-time link for the remainder of our session (we need about 90 minutes) and 2) can you confirm whether Redwood has an auto-reclaim policy for inactive ephemeral links (our security team wants to know the TTL and whether links are revoked automatically after inactivity or after N failed logins).

We have an audit window scheduled through Friday for Acme Financial Services and would prefer to avoid re-running collection. If an extended link isn't possible, a short bridge letter confirming the access gap and evidence preservation policy for the session would be sufficient for our audit notes.

Thanks — Maria
Maria Lopez
Senior IT Auditor
Diligence Partners
[m] +1 415-555-0186

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@diligencepartners.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access interruption during evidence download — request for extension and policy clarification

Maria — thanks for flagging and sorry about the interruption.

Short answers up front: we can issue a one-time SSO link with a 2-hour TTL that will not be re-used, and we do have an auto-reclaim policy that revokes ephemeral links after 15 minutes of inactivity by default. The TTL and the inactivity window are independently configurable for auditor sessions.

Here is what I can do right now:
- Issue a timeboxed one-time link valid for 2 hours (non-renewable) for your team; it will be IP-locked to the IPs you used this morning unless you request otherwise.
- Generate a short bridge letter that states the session interruption time range and confirms that our evidence storage is immutable for the audit period (we keep object checksums and access logs).

Ben — can you confirm whether we should temporarily relax the inactivity reclaim to 30 minutes for this session and whether we need to capture a separate access_log CSV for Maria's team?

Vanessa — I will need a signed bridge letter template if you have the standard language.
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@diligencepartners.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access interruption during evidence download — request for extension and policy clarification

Kim — putting the ops detail here.

We can flip the inactivity threshold from 15 -> 30 minutes for this Acme session and issue a one-time link with a 2-hour TTL. Changing the threshold is a config for the trust-portal session manager and will only apply to the session ID we create; no global policy change.

I'll also export the session access log (timestamps, IP, file object IDs) and attach a CSV. The export will include SHA-256 checksums for the downloaded evidence objects so Maria can match what she saw.

Attachment: portal_access_log_20260901.csv (session export, csv, ~38KB)

Please confirm if we should IP-lock to 52.24.10.77/32 and 18.205.33.12/32 (these were the auditor IPs today). If they will switch networks we won't IP-lock.

Ben
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@diligencepartners.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Bridge letter draft and one-time link (signed draft attached)

Hi Maria — attaching the bridge-letter draft that confirms the access interruption window and our evidence preservation statements. I signed the draft in PDF and included a version with the standard wording we use for SOC 2 sessions.

Attachment: bridge_letter_signed_draft.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

Kim/B — we will issue the one-time session now, TTL 2 hours, inactivity reclaim set to 30 minutes for the session. IP-locking: we will not enforce IP-locking unless Maria confirms; leaving unlocked for mobility.

One-time link (expired after use): https://trust.redwood.ai/session/one-time?token=XYZ-REDACTED

Maria — please confirm receipt of the PDF and whether you want IP-locking. If you accept, we'll also push the DocuSign envelope and provide the final signed bridge letter to attach to your audit package.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@diligencepartners.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge letter draft and one-time link (signed draft attached)

Thanks Vanessa — I received the link and the PDF. Downloaded the remaining samples successfully using the one-time session.

We do not need IP-locking; staying unlocked is fine. The bridge letter language looks good — please proceed with the final signing. One quick ask: can you also include the session export CSV in the signed bundle so we can reference exact download timestamps in our report?

If you can attach portal_access_log_20260901.csv to the final signed package (or include it as a separate signed artifact), that will close our internal evidence chain-of-custody check.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Maria
